Fit the SuSiE-OUT fine-mapping model

Source: R/fit.R
susieout_fit.Rd

Fit the SuSiE-OUT fine-mapping model

Usage

susieout_fit(
  z,
  n,
  R_analysis,
  wgs_ld = NULL,
  examined_ids = NULL,
  effect_prior = "robust_mixture",
  L = 10L,
  count_prior = susieout_count_prior(),
  infinitesimal_variance = 0,
  ld_mismatch_variance = 0,
  transform_wgs = TRUE,
  ridge = 1e-06,
  max_iter = 200L,
  tol = 1e-05,
  initialization = c("zero", "inside", "mixed"),
  trained_prior = NULL,
  inside_weights = NULL,
  outside_weights = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

z

Tested-variant z scores.

n

GWAS sample size.

R_analysis

Tested-variant analysis LD matrix. A Matrix sparse matrix invokes the scalable R + dI backend.

wgs_ld

A cross-LD matrix or list containing cross_ld, optional R_SS, and variant IDs/alleles.

examined_ids

IDs for tested variants.

effect_prior

A prior returned by susieout_effect_prior() or its name.

L

Maximum number of single-effect components.

count_prior

An L-invariant prior returned by susieout_count_prior().

infinitesimal_variance

Total local infinitesimal effect variance (local heritability). The corresponding z-score covariance multiplier is n * infinitesimal_variance / length(z).

ld_mismatch_variance

Fixed independent LD-mismatch variance.

transform_wgs

Apply whitening/recoloring when WGS R_SS is supplied.

ridge

Numerical ridge relative to the covariance scale.

max_iter

Maximum IBSS sweeps.

tol

Maximum fitted-mean change required for convergence.

initialization

Variational initialization. inside greedily seeds tested variants; mixed seeds tested variants and OUT states together.

trained_prior

Optional frozen object from susieout_train_prior().

inside_weights

Optional within-set prior weights.

outside_weights

Optional within-set prior weights.

...

Reserved; extra arguments are rejected.

Value

An object of class susieout_fit, a list that includes:

  • pip_in, pip_out: PIPs for tested variants and for omitted variants (OUT PIPs).

  • alpha_in, alpha_out: per-component assignment probabilities.

  • any_causal_omitted: posterior probability that at least one sparse effect is assigned to an omitted variant (locus OUT support), and candidate_set_complete, its complement.

  • component_null, component_outside: per-component null and OUT probabilities.

  • fitted, residual: fitted and residual z scores.

  • infinitesimal, ld_mismatch: nuisance variance settings.

  • diagnostics: convergence and numerical diagnostics.

Use susieout_candidate_support(), susieout_credible_sets() and summary() to summarize it.

References

Wang G, Sarkar A, Carbonetto P, Stephens M (2020). A simple new approach to variable selection in regression, with application to genetic fine mapping. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B 82, 1273–1300.

Examples

locus <- susieout_simulate_locus(1, architecture = "entirely_omitted")
fit <- susieout_fit(
  locus$z, locus$n, locus$R_analysis, locus$wgs_ld, locus$examined_ids,
  L = 10, count_prior = susieout_count_prior(1, out_fraction = 0.10)
)
fit$any_causal_omitted
#> [1] 0.1669364
head(susieout_candidate_support(fit))
#>     variant_id   state        pip maximum_component_probability
#> v40        v40  inside 0.04196349                   0.004277781
#> v28        v28  inside 0.03861921                   0.003930730
#> v29        v29  inside 0.02933064                   0.002972515
#> v41        v41 outside 0.02656404                   0.002688715
#> v44        v44 outside 0.02528099                   0.002557339
#> v43        v43 outside 0.02146891                   0.002167927
